summary: An EEG validation script was updated to replace a random train/test split with a LOSO-style subject split and to replace an invalid contrastive loss implementation with a symmetric InfoNCE-style objective. The review passed after resolving the previously identified train/test leakage and runtime error, with only non-blocking design warnings remaining.
datasets: Synthetic EEG toy dataset (5 subjects, 20 trials per subject)
lessons: Use subject-level splits for LOSO rather than random train/test splits.
Validate tensor dimensions to prevent runtime reduction errors.
Construct pairwise similarity matrices for InfoNCE instead of collapsing representations prematurely.
Treat temporal pooling as an explicit modeling assumption because it discards temporal information.
Avoid resetting the global random number generator inside reusable data-loading functions.
Toy synthetic datasets are useful for validation but are not substitutes for realistic EEG preprocessing or subject metadata.

summary: An EEG validation script was reviewed after replacing a random train/test split with a subject-level LOSO split and replacing an invalid contrastive loss with a symmetric InfoNCE-style objective. All previous blocking issues were resolved, resulting in a PASS with only non-blocking methodological and design warnings remaining.
datasets: Synthetic toy EEG dataset (5 subjects, 20 trials per subject)
lessons: Use subject-level splits for LOSO instead of random train/test splits to prevent subject leakage.
Construct pairwise similarity matrices for InfoNCE rather than collapsing representations before the contrastive objective.
Use realistic EEG datasets with subject metadata for research validation rather than relying solely on synthetic data.
Implement a complete LOSO evaluation by iterating over each subject as the held-out test subject rather than hard-coding a single split.

summary: Implemented confidence-aware MatchNet support for the KUL pipeline while preserving the existing model interface. The implementation passed review after correcting the confidence semantics to an uncalibrated probability proxy and maintaining compatibility with the validated InfoNCE training methodology.
lessons: Preserve model forward() interfaces when extending research models to avoid downstream runtime regressions.
Do not describe heuristic sigmoid-transformed similarity margins as calibrated confidence without an explicit calibration procedure.
Document temporal pooling as an explicit modeling assumption because it discards temporal information.
Factor shared similarity computations into a single implementation to keep training and inference behavior consistent.
Validate any confidence-based decision thresholds on held-out LOSO subjects using calibration metrics before interpreting them as uncertainty estimates.
Maintain pairwise InfoNCE similarity matrix construction when adding auxiliary confidence functionality to avoid altering the validated contrastive objective.

summary: Confidence-aware MatchNet support for the KUL pipeline was validated while preserving backward compatibility and the existing InfoNCE training methodology. The implementation passed review with no blocking issues, confirming that confidence is implemented as an auxiliary uncalibrated score derived from shared similarity computations.
lessons: Preserve the MatchNet forward() interface when extending models with auxiliary confidence outputs to maintain downstream compatibility.
Route all confidence computation through a shared similarity implementation to keep training, inference, and export behavior consistent.
Treat sigmoid-transformed similarity margins as monotonic confidence proxies rather than calibrated probabilities unless explicit calibration is performed.
Validate confidence quality on held-out LOSO subjects using reliability metrics before selecting confidence thresholds.
Keep the validated pairwise InfoNCE objective unchanged when adding confidence-related functionality.
Document temporal averaging as an explicit modeling assumption because it discards temporal structure.
Avoid accidentally replacing validated InfoNCE training with legacy margin-based contrastive losses when both implementations coexist in the codebase.
Treat confidence temperature as a heuristic scaling parameter unless it is explicitly learned or calibrated.
